rows.claim_summary: Systematic reviews confirm that adoption is slowed by fragmented data environments, limited explainability and a lack of prospective clinical evidence.
In cardiovascular applications, the literature reveals broad enthusiasm but few implementation case studies and no clear pathways for compliance with emerging AI regulations.
• KPI1.1: ≥1 multimodal AI model integrated with causal modules.
• KPI1.2: ≥10 clinicians test the tool and ≥80% report improved confidence in AI- supported decisions.
• KPI1.3: ≥1 joint report or white paper citing causal evidence generated within the project.
• KPI2.1: successful integration of ≥4 data modalities into a unified semantic schema.
• KPI2.2: ≥1 pilot model per use case integrating ≥3 formalised clinical or physiological rules.
• KPI2.3: ≥1 data exchange protocol between academic and industrial partners.
• KPI2.4: ≥1 published guideline or white paper reviewed by technical, clinical and regulatory stakeholders.
• KPI3.1: clinician and patient usability ratings ≥80%.
• KPI3.2: ≥2 co-design workshops with ≥15 participants.
• KPI3.3: ≥3 AI tools supporting interactive clinician feedback and retraining mechanisms.
• KPI4.1: ≥1 health-economic or cost-effectiveness evaluation.
• KPI4.2: ≥2 policy briefs or white papers.
• ≥1 regulatory-readiness toolkit publication.

• Within the first three months, the ITP and DC jointly agree a Personal Career Development Plan (PCDP), specifying research objectives, training needs, secondments, open-science commitments and career goals.

The PCDP is reviewed at least every six months and updated when needed; key milestones are aligned with host doctoral-school requirements and network deliverables, and PCDP updates are validated through the Supervisory Board as part of training monitoring activities.
• Regular meetings between DCs and their main supervisors (typically every 2–4 weeks) focus on scientific progress, skills development and well-being.
All DCs will complete a substantial secondment (4-6 months) in another sector, typically hosted by non-academic partners (hospitals, SMEs, large industry or regulatory/standardisation bodies).
Measurable outcomes include at least three joint doctoral courses, three transferable- skills modules and the majority (≥ 80%) of secondment months in non-academic settings.

Within their first three months, each Doctoral Candidate (DC) establishes a Personal Career Development Plan (PCDP) with their supervisory team, detailing research milestones, scientific and transferable-skills targets, secondments, teaching and outreach contributions, and short-, medium- and long-term career objectives.
Each doctoral candidate is expected to produce at least three peer-reviewed publications or conference contributions during the project, yielding a minimum of approximately 27 scientific outputs.

Task 1.1 - Fairness analysis of state-of-the-art AI models in specific populations: Underrepresented groups are often insufficiently represented in training data, leading to dataset shifts and performance disparities.

• Clinical registries and biobanks (Academic Beneficiary I): multimodal registries and biobanks combining clinical, biomarker, biosignal and imaging data, plus advanced electrophysiology, imaging and neurophysiology facilities supporting WP3–4 use cases.
These complementarities are embedded in the network’s design: each DC project combines at least two environments through co-supervision and international/intersectoral secondments.
Calls will remain open for at least one month, with deadline extensions and reinforced outreach if the applicant pool lacks gender balance or sufficient qualified candidates.

All calls will be launched at project start, the application window will run for at least one month, evaluation and interviews will follow immediately, and appointments are expected between months four and six.

A research and technology organisation linked to a world-leading technological university, with extensive participation in international collaborative research programmes and doctoral training initiatives.
